title: Sharpen org profile README opening to lead with logic-as-information-artifacts framing
description:
Rewrite the opening of the org profile README (`cmdrvl/.github/profile/README.md`, renders at github.com/cmdrvl) to lead with a sharper, more specific framing than the current "help agents answer hard data questions without hand-waving."

Target framing (validated in a 2026-09-03 LinkedIn exchange responding to a Vin post on AI/agents needing business logic as information models rather than embedded code): these tools externalize business logic — constraint sets (`verify`), registries (`canon`), schemas (`profile`), pattern definitions (`fingerprint`) — into declared, versioned, content-hashed artifacts instead of leaving it buried in application code or expecting an agent to infer it from a codebase it can't reliably query. The binaries themselves carry no embedded domain logic; 100% of the domain-specific behavior lives in the external artifact.

Keep the existing "What this feels like with an agent" before/after section and the two worked examples — those are good and concrete. Just sharpen the opening paragraph(s) so a first-time visitor immediately understands the tools are an implementation of "logic as information artifacts," not just "tools that reduce hand-waving."

Source: bd-3m5 audit, 2026-09-03.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
Direction refinement from Zac (2026-09-03):

- Drop the word "spine" from all these surfaces (README, system prompt, install/tool copy) — it's internal jargon that adds no value externally. Applies to `SPINE_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`'s title/body ("Epistemic Spine System Prompt", "epistemic spine") and any other public-facing copy that uses it. Rename the file itself as part of the bd-3bd fix (folds into that work).
- De-slopify the text: cut AI-generated-sounding filler, keep it simple and direct.
- Shift the framing: don't try to make the human-facing README fully explain every mechanism. Keep the human-facing surface short and simple, and explicitly encourage handing the details off to the reader's own coding agent (paste the system prompt in, let the agent read `--describe`/`--schema`) for full understanding — the agent-facing docs carry the depth, not the README.

title: Fix broken SYSTEM_PROMPT.md link in org profile README
description:
The org profile README (`cmdrvl/.github/profile/README.md`, "For Agent Builders" section) links to `./SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`, but the actual file is `SPINE_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md` — confirmed 404 via `gh api repos/cmdrvl/.github/contents/profile/SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`.

Fix: rename `SPINE_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md` -> `SYSTEM_PROMPT.md` (shorter, matches the README's existing link text "System Prompt" and the sibling `AGENT_PROMPT.md` naming convention) and update the README link accordingly. Alternative: keep the filename and fix the link instead — either is fine, just make them consistent.

While in the file, add `veil` and `airlock` to the install line and a one-line mention in the tool list — they're in the org README's Shipped Tools table but missing from the system prompt's install command and tool summary.

title: Audit and improve github.com/cmdrvl accessibility for agents and humans
description:
Audit and improve how github.com/cmdrvl and its agent-facing surfaces communicate the spine tools (vacuum, hash, fingerprint, profile, shape, rvl, verify, benchmark, assess, canon, lock, pack, veil, airlock, twinning, regret) — especially the framing that these tools work as business-logic-as-information-artifacts primitives for agents (constraint sets, registries, schemas, fingerprints — not embedded code logic), which is the angle that resonated in a recent LinkedIn exchange (Vin's "AI needs business logic as information models, not code" post, 2026-09-03).

Findings from initial audit (2026-09-03):

1. Org profile README (`cmdrvl/.github/profile/README.md`, renders at github.com/cmdrvl) is actually already fairly strong — has concrete examples, a "Start Here" table, quick start, and a "For Agent Builders" section. Opportunity: sharpen the opening framing to lead with "these tools externalize business logic into declared, versioned artifacts (constraint sets, registries, schemas) instead of leaving it embedded in code or expecting an agent to infer it" — this is a stronger, more specific hook than the current "help agents answer hard data questions without hand-waving" opener.

2. **Broken link, confirmed bug**: the README's "For Agent Builders" section links to `./SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`, but the actual file in the repo is named `SPINE_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md` (`cmdrvl/.github/profile/SPINE_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`) — a rename that never got the README link updated. Confirmed 404 via `gh api repos/cmdrvl/.github/contents/profile/SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`. `AGENT_PROMPT.md` (the other linked file) does exist and resolves fine.

3. The content of `SPINE_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md` itself is solid — compact (~38 lines), copy-paste-ready, covers the pipeline, report tools, refusal handling, self-discovery (`--describe`/`--schema`). Minor gap: it doesn't mention `veil` or `airlock` in the install line or tool list, even though the org README's Shipped Tools table does.

4. **cmdrvl.com already has a GitHub link** — present in the footer (`data-cmdrvl-footer-link="primary"` → `https://github.com/cmdrvl`) and in the homepage's schema.org `sameAs` JSON-LD. So "ensure github link on cmdrvl.com" is mostly done; worth a quick check on whether it should also be more prominent than footer-only (e.g., surfaced from a dedicated open-source/tools page or the main nav), given the open-source CLI layer is a distinct audience from the consulting/data-product visitors the rest of the site targets.

5. **Gap: cmdrvl.com's agent-facing surfaces (llms.txt, llms-full.txt) never mention the open-source spine tools at all.** Confirmed via `curl https://cmdrvl.com/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt` — both are entirely about the CMD+RVL consulting/data-product business (finance/procurement outcomes, evidence packs, MCP servers) with zero reference to github.com/cmdrvl, the spine tools, or a system-prompt link. An agent reading cmdrvl.com's own agent-facing index has no path to discover the open-source tools exist.

Scope for this epic: land the concrete fixes below, then re-review the whole surface end to end (org README opening framing, tool list completeness, cmdrvl.com llms.txt/llms-full.txt, and GitHub link prominence) against the accessibility bar Zac raised.
